source.text: וַיִּסְפֹּ֨ר שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֨לֶף֙ אִ֣ישׁ סַבָּ֔ל וּשְׁמוֹנִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ חֹצֵ֣ב בָּהָ֑ר וּמְנַצְּחִ֣ים עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And counted Solomon seventy thousand men bearing burdens and eighty thousand men hewing in the mountain, and overseeing over them three thousand and six hundred.

en.L: And Solomon counted out 70,000 men [to be] burden bearers and 80,000 men [to be] stonecutters in the hills, and 3,600 overseers over them.
en.B: Solomon assigned 70,000 men to carry loads and 80,000 men to cut stone in the hill country, and 3,600 to supervise them.
en.R: Solomon chose 70,000 men to carry loads and 80,000 men to cut stone in the hills. He also chose 3,600 men to be their foremen.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: this verse is 2:2 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 1 ends with verse 18, where Solomon decides to build a house for the name of Yahweh and a royal palace for himself. Many Bibles make that verse 2:1, and so number the verses of this chapter (2:1-17 here) 2:2-18. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: counted: counted off and assigned to the work
decisions.reason: The verb means to count. Here Solomon counts men off for a task. Verses 16-17 tell the same thing more fully: the workers were the outsiders living in the land, and Solomon counted them and assigned them to these tasks.

decisions.choice: 70,000, 80,000 and 3,600: as in verse 17; 1 Kings has 3,300 overseers
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 5:29-30 gives the same 70,000 carriers and 80,000 stonecutters, but 3,300 officers over the work. The two figures may count different ranks of supervisors, or one may have changed in copying. The Hebrew of each book is followed.

decisions.choice: overseers: men who directed the work
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to lead or supervise; Chronicles uses it of the Levites who oversaw the temple work (1 Chronicles 23:4; 2 Chronicles 34:12-13). These were foremen over the work gangs.

decisions.choice: counted out (Literal); assigned (Balanced); chose (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the counting was for (m2), and Readable adds "men" and "foremen" so the numbers are clear.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֶל־חוּרָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ־צֹ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ עִם־דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֔י וַתִּֽשְׁלַֽח־ל֣וֹ אֲרָזִ֔ים לִבְנֽוֹת־ל֥וֹ בַ֖יִת לָשֶׁ֥בֶת בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Solomon to Huram king of Tyre, saying, As you dealt with David my father and sent to him cedars to build for him a house to dwell in it,

en.L: And Solomon sent to Huram king of Tyre, saying, "As you dealt with David my father, and sent him cedars to build himself a house to dwell in, [so deal with me].
en.B: Solomon sent this message to Huram king of Tyre: "Deal with me as you dealt with my father David, when you supplied him with cedar for building a house to live in.
en.R: Solomon sent this message to Huram, the king of Tyre: "Please help me as you helped my father David. You sent him cedar logs to build a palace to live in.

decisions.choice: Huram king of Tyre: the Hiram of Samuel and Kings
decisions.reason: Chronicles spells the king's name Huram; Samuel and Kings spell it Hiram (2 Samuel 5:11; 1 Kings 5:15). Both are spellings of one name, and he is the same king. In 1 Kings 5:15-16 Hiram first sends envoys to Solomon; Chronicles begins with Solomon's message.

decisions.choice: as you dealt with David: the request is implied
decisions.reason: The sentence gives only the comparison, "as you dealt with David my father", and leaves the main clause unspoken. What Solomon asks is clear from what follows: deal with me in the same way, and send me timber and a craftsman (verses 6-7).

decisions.choice: cedars for David's house
decisions.reason: Hiram had sent cedar and craftsmen to build David's palace (2 Samuel 5:11; 1 Chronicles 14:1).

decisions.choice: [so deal with me] (Literal); Deal with me as (Balanced); Please help me as (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level supplies the request the Hebrew leaves unspoken (m2): Literal in brackets, Balanced and Readable in the sentence. Balanced and Readable also say "sent this message" for "sent ... saying", as at 1 Kings 5:16.

decisions.choice: palace (Readable)
decisions.reason: The house David lived in was his palace, and Readable says so.

source.text: הִנֵּה֩ אֲנִ֨י בֽוֹנֶה־בַּ֜יִת לְשֵׁ֣ם׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֗י לְהַקְדִּ֣ישׁ ל֡וֹ לְהַקְטִ֣יר לְפָנָ֣יו קְטֹֽרֶת־סַמִּים֩ וּמַעֲרֶ֨כֶת תָּמִ֤יד וְעֹלוֹת֙ לַבֹּ֣קֶר וְלָעֶ֔רֶב לַשַּׁבָּתוֹת֙ וְלֶ֣חֳדָשִׁ֔ים וּֽלְמוֹעֲדֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ לְעוֹלָ֖ם זֹ֥את עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Here I [am] building a house for [the] name of Yahweh my God, to consecrate [it] to him, to burn before him incense of spices, and [the] row continual, and burnt offerings for the morning and for the evening, for the sabbaths and for the new moons and for the appointed times of Yahweh our God; forever this [is] upon Israel.

en.L: Look, I am about to build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God, to dedicate [it] to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to burn fragrant incense before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and [for] the regular row [of bread], and [for] burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths and on the new moons and at the appointed feasts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. This [is] for Israel forever.
en.B: I am now going to build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God and dedicate it to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, for burning fragrant incense before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, for setting out the bread in rows regularly, and for burnt offerings every morning and evening, on Sabbaths, at new moons and at the appointed feasts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. This is a duty Israel is to keep forever.
en.R: I am going to build a temple to honor the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God. It will be set apart for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. There we will burn sweet-smelling incense to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and always keep the holy bread set out before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. We will offer burnt offerings every morning and evening, on Sabbath days, at each new moon, and at the festivals of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. Israel is to do this forever.

decisions.choice: a house for the name of Yahweh: the place where his name would dwell
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 5:17-19, the house is for Yahweh's name, the place Deuteronomy said he would choose for his name to live (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11). Verse 5 says why it can be no more than that.

decisions.choice: the regular row: the bread of the Presence
decisions.reason: The "row" is the bread laid out in rows on the gold table in the holy place and renewed every Sabbath (Leviticus 24:5-8; Exodus 25:30; 1 Chronicles 9:32). "Regular" means it was always there.

decisions.choice: incense, bread, burnt offerings, Sabbaths, new moons, feasts: the worship the law set out
decisions.reason: Solomon lists the regular worship of the law: incense on the gold altar (Exodus 30:7-8), the bread of the Presence, the burnt offerings of every morning and evening, and the offerings of Sabbaths, new moons and appointed feasts (Numbers 28-29). In 1 Kings 5:19 Solomon says only that he will build a house for Yahweh's name; Chronicles spells out what the house is for.

decisions.choice: forever this is upon Israel: a lasting duty laid on Israel
decisions.reason: "Upon Israel" means laid on Israel as a duty. The worship just listed is to be kept for all time.

decisions.choice: Look (Literal); not rendered (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "behold" draws attention to what Solomon is about to do; Balanced and Readable let the sentence carry it.

decisions.choice: temple; holy bread; festivals (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for the house, as 1 Kings does at this level, "holy bread" for the row of bread (m2), and "festivals" for the appointed feasts.

source.text: וְהַבַּ֛יִת אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֥י בוֹנֶ֖ה גָּד֑וֹל כִּֽי־גָד֥וֹל אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ מִכָּל־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And the house which I [am] building [will be] great, for great [is] our God above all the gods.

en.L: And the house that I am building [will be] great, for our God [is] great above all the gods.
en.B: The house I am building will be great, because our God is great above all gods.
en.R: The temple I am going to build will be great, since our God is far above every other god.

decisions.choice: great above all the gods: Yahweh is supreme over the gods of the nations
decisions.reason: Solomon writes to a king who served other gods, and says plainly that his God is above them all (Exodus 18:11; Psalm 95:3). The greatness of the house is to fit the greatness of the God it honors.

decisions.choice: great ... great: the same word twice
decisions.reason: The house will be great because God is great; the repeated word ties the two together. The second is a comparison, "great beyond" or "greater than" all gods.

decisions.choice: far above every other god (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the comparison (m2) in plain words.

source.text: וּמִ֤י יַעֲצָר־כֹּ֨חַ֙ לִבְנֽוֹת־ל֣וֹ בַ֔יִת כִּ֧י הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם וּשְׁמֵ֥י הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם לֹ֣א יְכַלְכְּלֻ֑הוּ וּמִ֤י אֲנִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶבְנֶה־לּ֣וֹ בַ֔יִת כִּ֖י אִם־לְהַקְטִ֥יר לְפָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: But who retains strength to build for him a house, for the heavens and [the] heavens of the heavens not contain him? And who [am] I that I should build for him a house, except to burn [offerings] before him?

en.L: But who is able to build {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a house, since the heavens and the heavens of the heavens cannot contain {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? And who [am] I that I should build {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a house, except to burn [offerings] before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?
en.B: But who is able to build a house for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, when heaven itself, even the highest heaven, cannot contain {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? Who am I, then, to build {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a house, except as a place to burn offerings before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?
en.R: But no one can really build a house for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Even the sky and the highest heaven cannot hold {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! So who am I to build a temple for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? It can only be a place where offerings are burned to honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: who retains strength: who is able
decisions.reason: To "retain strength" is to have the power to do something (1 Chronicles 29:14). The question expects the answer "no one".

decisions.choice: the heavens cannot contain him: Solomon's prayer at the dedication
decisions.reason: Solomon says the same at the dedication of the house: "the heavens and the heavens of the heavens cannot contain you" (1 Kings 8:27; 2 Chronicles 6:18). Here he says it before the building begins.

decisions.choice: the heavens of the heavens: the highest heaven
decisions.reason: The phrase means the heavens at their utmost, the whole of the heavens and beyond (Deuteronomy 10:14).

decisions.choice: to burn before him: a place for offerings, not a dwelling that holds God
alternatives: except to burn incense before him
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke, used for incense and for offerings burned on the altar. Solomon sees the house not as a home that holds God but as a place where Israel worships him. In verse 3 the same verb has incense as its object, and incense alone may be meant here.

decisions.choice: as a place to burn offerings (Balanced); a place where offerings are burned to honor him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "a place" and "offerings" to say what the house is for (m4).

decisions.choice: statements for the first question (Readable)
decisions.reason: The first question means "no one can" (m1), and Readable says that directly; it keeps the second question, which Solomon asks of himself.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה שְֽׁלַֽח־לִ֣י אִישׁ־חָכָ֡ם לַעֲשׂוֹת֩ בַּזָּהָ֨ב וּבַכֶּ֜סֶף וּבַנְּחֹ֣שֶׁת וּבַבַּרְזֶ֗ל וּבָֽאַרְגְּוָן֙ וְכַרְמִ֣יל וּתְכֵ֔לֶת וְיֹדֵ֖עַ לְפַתֵּ֣חַ פִּתּוּחִ֑ים עִם־הַֽחֲכָמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר עִמִּי֙ בִּֽיהוּדָ֣ה וּבִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵכִ֖ין דָּוִ֥יד אָבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And now send to me a man skilled to work in gold and in silver and in bronze and in iron and in purple and crimson and violet, and knowing to engrave engravings, with the skilled [ones] who [are] with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom provided David my father.

en.L: And now send me a man skilled to work in gold and in silver and in bronze and in iron, and in purple and crimson and blue [yarn], and who knows how to engrave engravings, [to work] with the skilled men who [are] with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father provided.
en.B: So now send me a man skilled in working with gold, silver, bronze and iron, and with purple, crimson and blue yarn, who also knows how to engrave. He will work with the skilled craftsmen I have here in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.
en.R: So please send me a skilled craftsman. He must know how to work with gold, silver, bronze and iron, and with purple, red and blue cloth, and how to carve designs. He will work with the skilled workers my father David arranged for me here in Judah and Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: purple, crimson and blue: costly dyed yarns
decisions.reason: These are the rich colored threads used for the curtains and garments of the sanctuary (Exodus 26:1; 28:5). The word for crimson is found only in Chronicles (here, verse 13 and 3:14) and names a deep red dye; the tabernacle passages use another word for scarlet. The word for purple is a later spelling of the one in Exodus.

decisions.choice: engrave engravings: carving designs
decisions.reason: The verb and noun are used for engraving stones and metal plates (Exodus 28:9-11, 36) and for carving wood (1 Kings 6:29).

decisions.choice: the skilled men David provided
decisions.reason: David had gathered masons, carpenters and craftsmen of every kind for the temple before he died (1 Chronicles 22:15-16; 28:21).

decisions.choice: skilled: wise in a craft
decisions.reason: The word usually rendered "wise" is used of skill in a craft, as of the craftsmen of the tabernacle (Exodus 31:6; 35:10).

decisions.choice: yarn (Literal in brackets, Balanced); cloth, red (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names only the colors; the materials were dyed yarn and the cloth woven from it (m1). Readable says "red" for crimson.

source.text: וּֽשְׁלַֽח־לִי֩ עֲצֵ֨י אֲרָזִ֜ים בְּרוֹשִׁ֣ים וְאַלְגּוּמִּים֮ מֵֽהַלְּבָנוֹן֒ כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יָדַ֔עְתִּי אֲשֶׁ֤ר עֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ יֽוֹדְעִ֔ים לִכְר֖וֹת עֲצֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן וְהִנֵּ֥ה עֲבָדַ֖י עִם־עֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And send to me timber of cedars, cypresses and algums from the Lebanon, for I know that your servants know to cut [the] timber of Lebanon; and here, my servants [will be] with your servants,

en.L: And send me timber of cedar, cypress and algum from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut the timber of Lebanon. And see, my servants [will be] with your servants,
en.B: Send me cedar, cypress and algum logs from Lebanon too, for I know that your servants are skilled at cutting the timber of Lebanon. My servants will work with your servants,
en.R: Please also send me cedar, cypress and algum logs from the Lebanon mountains. I know that your workers are experts at cutting down trees there. My workers will work beside yours.

decisions.choice: algum: a costly wood that cannot be identified with certainty
decisions.reason: This is the wood called almug in 1 Kings 10:11-12; Chronicles spells it algum here and in 9:10-11. There it is brought from Ophir by sea; here Solomon asks for it from Lebanon. Either more than one tree went by the name, or the name covered fine timber from both sources. The tree cannot be named with certainty.

decisions.choice: cypress: a tall evergreen, perhaps juniper or fir
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 5:22, the tree cannot be named with certainty; it was a strong evergreen of Lebanon used with cedar.

decisions.choice: your servants know how to cut timber
decisions.reason: In 1 Kings 5:20 Solomon says that no one among Israel knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians; Chronicles says the same thing from the other side, praising Huram's men. Both accounts have Solomon's men work beside Huram's.

decisions.choice: servants (Literal, Balanced); workers (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 5:20, Readable names these servants by the work they do.

decisions.choice: comma at the end of the verse (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on into verse 8, "to prepare timber for me"; Readable ends its own sentence here.

source.text: וּלְהָכִ֥ין לִ֛י עֵצִ֖ים לָרֹ֑ב כִּ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֥י בוֹנֶ֖ה גָּד֥וֹל וְהַפְלֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: and to prepare for me timber in abundance, for the house which I [am] building [will be] great and wonderful.

en.L: to prepare timber for me in abundance, for the house that I am building [will be] great and wonderful.
en.B: to get plenty of timber ready for me, because the house I am going to build will be great and wonderful.
en.R: Together they will prepare plenty of timber for me, because the temple I am going to build will be large and wonderful.

decisions.choice: to prepare: the work the two crews will do together
decisions.reason: The verb continues verse 7: Solomon's men and Huram's men are to work together to get the timber ready.

decisions.choice: great and wonderful: wonderfully great
decisions.reason: The second word is a verb form meaning "to do wonders", used here like an adverb: the house will be great in a way that makes people wonder.

decisions.choice: Together they will prepare (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and supplies its subject, the workers of verse 7 (m1).

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה לַֽחֹטְבִ֣ים׀לְֽכֹרְתֵ֣י׀הָעֵצִ֡ים נָתַתִּי֩ חִטִּ֨ים׀מַכּ֜וֹת לַעֲבָדֶ֗יךָ כֹּרִים֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אֶ֔לֶף וּשְׂעֹרִ֕ים כֹּרִ֖ים עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אָ֑לֶף וְיַ֗יִן בַּתִּים֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אֶ֔לֶף וְשֶׁ֕מֶן בַּתִּ֖ים עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אָֽלֶף׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And here, to the hewers, to [the] cutters of the trees, I will give wheat, crushed, for your servants, twenty thousand cors, and barley twenty thousand cors, and wine twenty thousand baths, and oil twenty thousand baths.

en.L: And see, to the woodsmen who cut the trees, your servants, I will give 20,000 cors of crushed wheat, and 20,000 cors of barley, and 20,000 baths of wine, and 20,000 baths of oil."
en.B: I will give your servants, the woodsmen who cut the timber, {{units:about 120,000 bushels|20,000 cors}} of crushed wheat, {{units:about 120,000 bushels|20,000 cors}} of barley, {{units:about 120,000 gallons|20,000 baths}} of wine and {{units:about 120,000 gallons|20,000 baths}} of oil."
en.R: For your workers who cut down the trees, I will provide {{units:about 120,000 bushels|20,000 cors}} of ground wheat, {{units:about 120,000 bushels|20,000 cors}} of barley, {{units:about 120,000 gallons|20,000 baths}} of wine and {{units:about 120,000 gallons|20,000 baths}} of olive oil."

decisions.choice: crushed wheat, as the Hebrew reads
alternatives: wheat as food for your servants
decisions.reason: The word after "wheat" is the plural of a word that usually means blows or wounds, and is taken here as "crushed", that is, ground or beaten grain. The parallel in 1 Kings 5:25 has a similar word meaning "food", and one letter's difference would give that word here: "wheat as food for your servants". The Hebrew as it stands is followed.

decisions.choice: the payment: different from 1 Kings 5:25
decisions.reason: In 1 Kings 5:25 Solomon gives Hiram 20,000 cors of wheat as food for his royal household and twenty cors of beaten oil each year. Here Solomon promises wheat, barley, wine and oil for the woodcutters, with 20,000 baths of oil. The two accounts may describe two parts of one bargain: food for Hiram's court and rations for the men in the forest.

decisions.choice: cors and baths
decisions.reason: The cor is the largest dry measure, about 6 bushels (1 Kings 5:2). The bath is a liquid measure, a tenth of a cor (Ezekiel 45:14), about 6 gallons.

decisions.choice: the woodcutters are Huram's servants
decisions.reason: "To the hewers, to the cutters of the trees" and "for your servants" name the same men: Huram's woodcutters in Lebanon.

decisions.choice: woodsmen (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: The word means hewers; with "cutters of the trees" beside it, "woodsmen" says who they were. Readable folds both into "workers who cut down the trees".

decisions.choice: ground wheat; olive oil (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "ground" for crushed and names the olive, as 1 Kings 5:25 does at this level.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר חוּרָ֤ם מֶֽלֶךְ־צֹר֙ בִּכְתָ֔ב וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה בְּאַהֲבַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֶת־עַמּ֔וֹ נְתָנְךָ֥ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֶֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Huram king of Tyre in writing, and he sent to Solomon: In [the] love of Yahweh his people he has made you over them king.

en.L: And Huram king of Tyre said in a letter, and he sent [it] to Solomon, "Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loves {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made you king over them."
en.B: Huram king of Tyre answered in a letter that he sent to Solomon: "Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loves {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made you their king."
en.R: Huram, the king of Tyre, wrote a letter back to Solomon. He said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} loves {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. That is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made you their king."

decisions.choice: in writing: a letter
decisions.reason: The word means something written, a document. Huram's reply is a written letter, as was usual between kings (2 Kings 5:5-7).

decisions.choice: in the love of Yahweh his people: because Yahweh loves his people
decisions.reason: The phrase gives the reason Solomon is king. The queen of Sheba says nearly the same (1 Kings 10:9; 2 Chronicles 9:8).

decisions.choice: a foreign king speaks of Yahweh
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 5:21, Huram speaks respectfully of Israel's God by name, in the courtesy of alliances; the words do not say that he left his own gods.

decisions.choice: quote marks close at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: Verse 11 begins again "And Huram said", so the words of this verse are closed here and verse 11 opens a new quotation from the same letter.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ חוּרָם֒ בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַן֩ לְדָוִ֨יד הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ בֵּ֣ן חָכָ֗ם יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙ שֵׂ֣כֶל וּבִינָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִבְנֶה־בַּ֨יִת֙ לַיהוָ֔ה וּבַ֖יִת לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Huram, Blessed [be] Yahweh, [the] God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth, who has given to David the king a son wise, knowing insight and understanding, who will build a house for Yahweh and a house for his kingdom.

en.L: And Huram said, "Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth, who has given to David the king a wise son, knowing insight and understanding, who will build a house for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and a house for his kingdom.
en.B: Huram also said, "Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, maker of heaven and earth, who has given King David a wise son, full of insight and understanding, who will build a house for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and a royal palace for himself.
en.R: Huram also said, "Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, who made the sky and the earth! He has given King David a wise son who has good sense and understanding. This son will build a temple for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and a palace for himself as king.

decisions.choice: Blessed be Yahweh who has given David a wise son: Hiram's words in 1 Kings 5:21, with more
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 5:21 has Hiram bless Yahweh "who has given to David a wise son over this great people". Chronicles adds that Yahweh is the God of Israel who made heaven and earth, that the son has insight and understanding, and that he will build a house for Yahweh and a palace for himself.

decisions.choice: knowing insight and understanding: having good sense and discernment
decisions.reason: To "know" insight is to have it. The first word means prudence or good sense (1 Samuel 25:3); the second is the discernment Solomon asked for (1 Kings 3:9-12).

decisions.choice: a house for his kingdom: a royal palace
decisions.reason: "A house for his kingship" is the king's palace, the house Solomon decided to build beside the house for Yahweh's name (1:18).

decisions.choice: Praise (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 5:21: to bless Yahweh means to praise and thank him.

decisions.choice: also said (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: These words are part of the same letter as verse 10, and "also" makes that clear. The quotation runs to the end of verse 15.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה שָׁלַ֧חְתִּי אִישׁ־חָכָ֛ם יוֹדֵ֥עַ בִּינָ֖ה לְחוּרָ֥ם אָבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And now I have sent a man skilled, knowing understanding, Huram-abi,

en.L: And now I have sent a skilled man, endowed with understanding, Huram-abi,
en.B: I am now sending you a skilled man who has understanding, Huram-abi,
en.R: I am sending you Huram-abi, a skilled man who has great understanding.

decisions.choice: Huram-abi: a name, or "Huram my father" as a title
decisions.reason: The word data reads the two words as one name, Huram-abi. The second word means "my father", and some take the phrase as "Huram my master", "father" being a title of honor for an adviser or master craftsman (Genesis 45:8). 4:16 calls the same man "Huram his father". 1 Kings 7:13 calls him Hiram.

decisions.choice: I have sent: sent with this letter
decisions.reason: In letters the past tense is used for what the writer does as he writes: Huram is sending the craftsman now, with his reply.

decisions.choice: I am now sending you (Balanced); I am sending you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the present tense the letter means (m2).

decisions.choice: comma at the end of the verse (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: The description of the craftsman goes on in verse 13; Readable ends its sentence here.

source.text: בֶּן־אִשָּׁ֞ה מִן־בְּנ֣וֹת דָּ֗ן וְאָבִ֣יו אִישׁ־צֹרִ֡י יוֹדֵ֡עַ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת בַּזָּֽהָב־וּ֠בַכֶּסֶף בַּנְּחֹ֨שֶׁת בַּבַּרְזֶ֜ל בָּאֲבָנִ֣ים וּבָעֵצִ֗ים בָּאַרְגָּמָ֤ן בַּתְּכֵ֨לֶת֙ וּבַבּ֣וּץ וּבַכַּרְמִ֔יל וּלְפַתֵּ֨חַ֙ כָּל־פִּתּ֔וּחַ וְלַחְשֹׁ֖ב כָּל־מַחֲשָׁ֑בֶת אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִנָּֽתֶן־לוֹ֙ עִם־חֲכָמֶ֔יךָ וְֽחַכְמֵ֔י אֲדֹנִ֖י דָּוִ֥יד אָבִֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: [the] son of a woman from [the] daughters of Dan, and his father [was] a man of Tyre, knowing to work in gold and in silver, in bronze, in iron, in stones and in wood, in purple, in violet and in fine linen and in crimson, and to engrave any engraving and to devise any design that will be given to him, with your skilled [ones] and [the] skilled [ones] of my lord David your father.

en.L: the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father [was] a man of Tyre. He knows how to work in gold and in silver, in bronze, in iron, in stone and in wood, in purple, in blue and in fine linen and in crimson, and to engrave any engraving and to devise any design that may be given to him, with your skilled men and the skilled men of my lord David your father.
en.B: the son of a woman from the tribe of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre. He is trained to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, and in purple, blue and crimson yarn and fine linen. He can engrave any kind of design and carry out any plan that is given to him. He will work with your craftsmen and with the craftsmen of my lord David, your father.
en.R: His mother was from the tribe of Dan, and his father was a man from Tyre. He knows how to work with gold, silver, bronze and iron, with stone and wood, and with purple, blue and red cloth and fine linen. He can carve any kind of design and make anything he is asked to make. He will work with your skilled workers and with those of my lord David, your father.

decisions.choice: a woman of Dan: 1 Kings 7:14 says a widow of Naphtali
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:14 says the craftsman's mother was a widow from the tribe of Naphtali; here she is a woman "of the daughters of Dan". She may have been born a Danite and married into Naphtali, or have lived in the town of Dan, which lay in the far north near Naphtali's land (Judges 18:29). The text does not say. Both accounts agree that his father was a man of Tyre.

decisions.choice: my lord David: a courteous title
decisions.reason: Huram calls David "my lord" and Solomon "my lord" (verse 14), the polite speech of an ally, not a claim that he served them.

decisions.choice: to devise any design: like Bezalel
decisions.reason: The words recall Bezalel, the craftsman of the tabernacle, whom God filled with skill "to devise designs" and to work in gold, silver, bronze, stone and wood (Exodus 31:3-5; 35:32-35). The list here is longer than Solomon's request in verse 6: it adds stone, wood and fine linen.

decisions.choice: fine linen: a word used in the later books
decisions.reason: The word names fine white linen, used in Chronicles for the clothing of the Levite singers and the temple curtain (1 Chronicles 15:27; 2 Chronicles 3:14).

decisions.choice: from the tribe of Dan (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "The daughters of Dan" means the women of that tribe; Balanced and Readable say so. Readable says "red" for crimson and "cloth" for the dyed materials, as in verse 6.

source.text: וְ֠עַתָּה הַחִטִּ֨ים וְהַשְּׂעֹרִ֜ים הַשֶּׁ֤מֶן וְהַיַּ֨יִן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנִ֔י יִשְׁלַ֖ח לַעֲבָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And now the wheat and the barley, the oil and the wine which said my lord, let him send to his servants.

en.L: And now the wheat and the barley, the oil and the wine, of which my lord has spoken, let him send to his servants.
en.B: So now let my lord send his servants the wheat and barley, the oil and wine, that he has promised.
en.R: So now, my lord, please send us the wheat and barley, the olive oil and the wine you promised.

decisions.choice: my lord ... his servants: polite speech between kings
decisions.reason: Huram speaks of Solomon as "my lord" and of his own woodcutters as Solomon's "servants", in the third person. This is the courtesy of the time, as in "your servant" for oneself (1 Samuel 20:7-8), not a statement that Huram's men belonged to Solomon.

decisions.choice: which my lord has said: which he has promised
decisions.reason: Huram means the food Solomon promised for the woodcutters in verse 9.

decisions.choice: you; us (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the polite third person into "you" and "us" so the request is clear (m1), keeping "my lord" as the address. Balanced and Literal keep "his servants".

source.text: וַ֠אֲנַחְנוּ נִכְרֹ֨ת עֵצִ֤ים מִן־הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ כְּכָל־צָרְכֶּ֔ךָ וּנְבִיאֵ֥ם לְךָ֛ רַפְסֹד֖וֹת עַל־יָ֣ם יָפ֑וֹ וְאַתָּ֛ה תַּעֲלֶ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And we will cut timber from the Lebanon according to all your need, and we will bring them to you [as] rafts on [the] sea [to] Joppa, and you will take them up [to] Jerusalem.

en.L: And we will cut logs from Lebanon, as much as you need, and we will bring them to you [as] rafts by sea [to] Joppa, and you will take them up [to] Jerusalem."
en.B: We will cut all the logs you need from Lebanon and bring them to you as rafts by sea to Joppa. From there you can take them up to Jerusalem."
en.R: We will cut all the logs you need in the mountains of Lebanon. We will tie them into rafts and float them along the coast to Joppa. Then you can carry them up to Jerusalem."

decisions.choice: rafts: logs tied together and floated
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It names floats of logs bound together; 1 Kings 5:23 uses a different word for the same thing.

decisions.choice: Joppa: the port named
decisions.reason: In 1 Kings 5:23 Hiram leaves the place to Solomon to name; Chronicles names it. Joppa was the port on the coast nearest Jerusalem (Jonah 1:3; Ezra 3:7), and from it the timber was carried up into the hills.

decisions.choice: you will take them up: Solomon's part
decisions.reason: The written-out "you" marks the change of task: Huram's men bring the timber to the coast, and Solomon's men carry it up to Jerusalem, as in 1 Kings 5:23.

decisions.choice: tie them into rafts; float them along the coast (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 5:23, Readable spells out how the rafts were made and moved (m1).

source.text: וַיִּסְפֹּ֣ר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה כָּל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הַגֵּירִים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֣י הַסְּפָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר סְפָרָ֖ם דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֑יו וַיִּמָּצְא֗וּ מֵאָ֤ה וַחֲמִשִּׁים֙ אֶ֔לֶף וּשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And counted Solomon all the men, the sojourners who [were] in [the] land of Israel, after the census which had counted them David his father; and they were found [to be] a hundred and fifty thousand and three thousand and six hundred.

en.L: And Solomon counted all the men, the sojourners who [were] in the land of Israel, after the census with which David his father had counted them; and they were found [to be] 153,600.
en.B: Solomon took a census of all the outsiders who lived in the land of Israel, after the one his father David had taken, and they came to 153,600.
en.R: Solomon counted all the outsiders living in the land of Israel, as his father David had counted them before. There were 153,600 of them.

decisions.choice: sojourners: people of other descent living in Israel
decisions.reason: The word names people living in a land not their own, without an inheritance in it. Here they are the peoples left in the land from before Israel, whom Solomon put to forced labor (1 Kings 9:20-21; 2 Chronicles 8:7-8).

decisions.choice: after the census David had taken: 1 Chronicles 22:2
alternatives: following the pattern of David's census
decisions.reason: David had gathered the outsiders in the land and set them to cut stone for the house of God (1 Chronicles 22:2). Solomon counts them again. "After" may mean later than David's census or following its pattern; the sense is much the same.

decisions.choice: who the workers were: Chronicles and 1 Kings
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 5:27-28 tells of 30,000 men raised from all Israel to work in Lebanon in shifts; Chronicles does not mention them. It says the 150,000 carriers and stonecutters were outsiders, which agrees with 1 Kings 9:20-22.

decisions.choice: sojourners (Literal); outsiders (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: These books say "outsider" at Balanced and Readable for this word, keeping "foreigner" for a different word (m1).

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ מֵהֶ֜ם שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֨לֶף֙ סַבָּ֔ל וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף חֹצֵ֣ב בָּהָ֑ר וּשְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת מְנַצְּחִ֖ים לְהַעֲבִ֥יד אֶת־הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made of them seventy thousand bearers of burdens and eighty thousand hewing in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred overseers to make work the people.

en.L: And he made 70,000 of them burden bearers, and 80,000 stonecutters in the hills, and 3,600 overseers to make the people work.
en.B: He assigned 70,000 of them to carry loads and 80,000 to cut stone in the hill country, and 3,600 to supervise them and keep the people at work.
en.R: He put 70,000 of them to work carrying loads and 80,000 cutting stone in the hills. He made 3,600 of them foremen to keep the people working.

decisions.choice: the numbers of verse 1 again
decisions.reason: Verse 1 gives the same three numbers; the account of the letters is set between the two. The 3,600 overseers differ from the 3,300 of 1 Kings 5:30 (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: to make the people work: to keep them at their labor
decisions.reason: The verb is the causative of "to work" or "to serve": the overseers saw that the people did the work. "The people" here are the workers just counted.

decisions.choice: of them: all three groups were outsiders
decisions.reason: "Of them" covers the overseers as well as the carriers and stonecutters. 1 Kings 5:30 calls the overseers Solomon's officers and does not say where they came from.

decisions.choice: foremen (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, Readable calls the overseers foremen.
